content: 143 meters when using the international inch standard. This unit was primarily employed in the tailoring industry but has since become obsolete. The ell was based on the length of the human arm, specifically the distance from the shoulder (or elbow) to the wrist. Various countries had their own versions of the ell, each with differing lengths.78 meters, or roughly 31 inches. In some contexts, the term ell was used interchangeably with cubit, another historical unit of length. During the reign of Edward I of England, it was mandated that every town possess an ell-wand for standardization purposes. In Scotland, the Belt of Orion constellation was colloquially referred to as the King's Ellwand.
